blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Annotators from different demographic backgrounds often disagree in systematic ways due to varying lived experiences, cultural contexts, and their relationship to the content. When such disagreement occurs, one group's perspective may sometimes warrant prioritization because they hold an epistemically advantaged standpoint or bear greater stake in the outcome. For example, when assessing toxicity of posts on social media, it may be important to prioritize a targeted group's viewpoint. We propose a Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework to jointly model demographic disagreement both across- and within- annotator groups. The model uses conditional gradient routing to handle sparsity induced by group-conditional labeling, and parameterization supports customized weighting of groups in different task settings. SAJ-MTL improves group-level performance in toxicity detection through better context-aware understanding of demographic-sensitive content. Only annotator group-membership information is required, which is more practical than existing methods requiring more privacy-invasive individual-level annotator details. Our scalable architecture is also computationally efficient to support large-scale deployment.
blocks.zh: 来自不同人口背景的注释者往往由于不同的生活经验、文化背景及其与内容的关系而系统地不同意。 当出现这种分歧时,一个集团的观点有时可能需要优先处理,因为它们具有明显的优势或对结果有更大的利害关系。 例如,在评估社交媒体帖子的毒性时,将目标群体的观点列为优先事项可能很重要。 我们建议建立一个利益攸关方-知情联合多任务学习框架,以联合模拟各说明群体之间和内部的人口分歧。 该模型使用有条件的梯度路由处理由组条件标签所诱发的痉挛,参数化支持不同任务环境下组的定制加权. SAJ-MTL通过更好地了解人口敏感含量,提高了组群在毒性检测方面的性能. 仅需要注释者团体会员信息,这比现有方法更实用,需要更多隐私入侵的个人层面注释者细节. 我们的可扩展架构在计算上也具有支持大规模部署的效率。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Across many machine learning tasks, annotator judgments vary by demographic group [ 63 ] .
Such disagreements depend not only on annotator demographics, but also on the critical relationship between the annotator identity and the group for whom the content is most relevant or familiar [ 17 ] . In medical diagnosis, Black and Latinx physicians in the US are historically more likely to serve in predominantly Black and Latinx communities [ 35 ] , and therefore may develop more expertise on the conditions that prevail in these communities and on how symptoms present. In a different domain of annotating online discourse, the sentiment of the phrase “quite good” depends on whether the speaker is British or American, as well as the annotator’s familiarity with the idioms [ 39 ] . From stove design [ 21 ] to content moderation [ 64 ] , judgment decisions are often highly context-dependent and significantly influenced
by an annotator’s relationship to the content. Thus, when annotating for such highly subjective tasks, one must not only be cognizant and intentional about the relation between annotators and content, but when faced with disagreement, prioritizing certain viewpoints often becomes particularly essential in practice.
blocks.zh:
在许多机器学习任务中,注释员的判断因人口群体而异 [63].
这种分歧不仅取决于注释者的人口统计,还取决于注释者身份与内容最相关或最熟悉的群体之间的关键关系[17]。 在医学诊断方面,美国黑人和拉丁裔医生在历史上更有可能在以黑人和拉丁裔为主的社区服务[35],因此可以对这些社区普遍存在的条件和症状的出现发展更多的专业知识. 在注解在线话语的不同领域,“相当好”一词的情绪取决于演讲者是英国人还是美国人,以及注释者对平话的熟悉程度[39]。 从炉子设计[21]到内容节制[64],判决往往高度依赖背景,并受到很大影响.

blocks.en: Early crowdsourcing work predominantly treated disagreement as annotator noise to be minimized, collapsing multiple judgments into a single “ground truth” via majority vote [ 57 , 34 , 45 ] . However, there is growing recognition that subjective annotation tasks [ 62 , 43 ] such as toxicity detection [ 53 ] , stance identification [ 24 ] , and sentiment analysis [ 6 ] are shaped by genuine differences in how demographic groups interpret content. Thus, a growing literature now argues that disagreement encodes meaningful social variation, and choices for how to handle disagreement are value-laden [ 20 ] . Fazelpour and De-Arteaga [17] adopt a standpoint theory lens [ 29 ] to posit that the relationship between annotator identity and the content being annotated is a crucial dimension through which sociocultural identity and diversity is relevant to the machine learning pipeline. Empirical evidence lends support to this perspective. For example, Davani et al. [11] empirically demonstrate that majority aggregation systematically erases minority viewpoints, a concern also raised on conceptual grounds by Noble [44] , while [ 22 , 54 , 46 ] show that disagreement often reflects important structured group- and individual-level differences.
blocks.zh: 早期的众包工作主要将分歧视为应尽量减少的注解噪音,通过多数表决将多项判决变成单一的“基本事实”[57、34、45]。 然而,人们日益认识到,主观注释的任务[62,43],如毒性检测[53],姿势识别[24],情绪分析[6],是由人口群体如何解释内容的真正差异决定的. 因此,现在越来越多的文献认为,分歧是有意义的社会差异的编码,如何处理分歧的选择是有价值的[20]。 Fazelpour和De-Arteaga [17] 采用了一个观点理论透镜[29],假定注释者身份与附加说明的内容之间的关系是一个关键维度,通过这个维度,社会文化身份和多样性与机器学习管道相关。 经验证据支持这一观点。 例如,达瓦尼等人. [11] 实证表明,多数汇总系统地消除了少数群体的观点,诺贝尔[44] 基于概念理由也提出了关切,而[22、54、46] 表明分歧往往反映了重要的结构化群体和个人层面的差异。

blocks.en: While some works have tied annotator identity directly into models, this is typically done broadly as an auxiliary signal, not as a principled source of epistemic variation [ 70 , 50 , 32 , 65 ] . Most existing methods considering annotator identity do not fully account for how the annotator-content relationship influences subjective judgments. This gap has been acknowledged in the literature; Binns [4] highlights that although some perspectives carry greater epistemic authority in fairness-critical settings, current modeling pipelines lack capabilities to explicitly operationalize such prioritization. Fleisig et al. [19] , a notable exception, attempts richer modeling of annotator variation. To do this, however, it requires fine-grained individual-level data or surveys, which raises significant privacy concerns and is often infeasible because such fine-grained data is rarely available. Overall, we perceive an unmet need for a framework that: (1) models both across-group and within-group disagreements explicitly; (2) enables dynamic, context-dependent viewpoint prioritization; and (3) remains computationally tractable without requiring privacy-invasive individual annotator-level features. This modeling space remains underexplored, lacking architectures that embed disagreement and socially grounded prioritization into the predictive pipeline itself.
blocks.zh: 虽然一些作品将注释者身份直接捆绑在模型中,但这通常作为辅助信号而广泛进行,而不是作为认知变化的原则来源[70,50,32,65]. 考虑注释者身份的大多数现有方法并未充分说明注释者-内容关系如何影响主观判断. 文献中承认了这一差距;宾斯[4]强调指出,虽然某些观点在公正的关键环境中具有更大的认知权威,但目前的建模管道缺乏明确实施这种优先顺序的能力。 Fleisig等人著. [19],一个值得注意的例外,试图对注释器变异进行更丰富的模型化. 然而,为了做到这一点,它需要精细的个人一级数据或调查,这引起了重大的隐私关切,而且往往不可行,因为很少获得这种精细的数据。 总体而言,我们认为,需要建立一个框架,使:(1) 明确模拟跨组和组内分歧;(2) 能够确定动态的、视具体情况而定的观点的优先次序;以及(3) 仍然可以计算,而不需要隐私入侵的个人注释员一级特征。 这一建模空间仍然未得到充分探索,缺乏将分歧和基于社会的优先安排嵌入预测管道本身的架构。

blocks.en: To address these challenges, we propose a novel multi-task learning (MTL) architecture, Stakeholder-Aware Joint MTL ( SAJ-MTL ), that explicitly models interactions between annotator and target demographics to model context-dependent weights on socially-grounded perspectives. SAJ-MTL treats annotator–target relationships as primary signals rather than incidental metadata. In regard to challenge (1) above, instead of smoothing away disagreement, the model captures both across-group and within-group disagreements via two protocols: Across-Groups (AG) vs. Across-and-Within-Groups (AWG). By conditioning model predictions on annotator and target identities, the framework preserves multiple perspectives rather than collapsing them into a single label. As for challenge (2) , SAJ-MTL enables dynamic viewpoint prioritization by allowing the model to integrate weighting functions that reflect epistemic authority, democratic considerations of representation, or task-specific priorities, rather than assuming a single canonical perspective. Finally, for challenge (3) , SAJ-MTL achieves tractable computation by factorizing annotator and target representations into an additive MTL architecture. Avoiding the quadratic explosion of per-pair modeling enables the framework to handle many stakeholder groups without sacrificing predictive performance and memory stagnation.
blocks.zh: 为了应对这些挑战,我们建议建立一个新的多任务学习架构,即利益攸关方-阿瓦雷联合MTL(SAJ-MTL),明确模拟注释者与目标人口学之间的相互作用,以模型化基于社会背景的视具体情况而定的权重。 SAJ-MTL将注释者-目标关系视为主信号而非附带元数据. 关于上述挑战(1),该模型没有平息分歧,而是通过两项协议捕捉到跨组和组内分歧: 跨集团(AG)对跨集团(AWG). 通过在注释器和目标身份上调节模型预测,框架保留了多个视角,而不是将其折叠成一个单一的标签. 至于挑战(2),SAJ-MTL通过允许该模型整合能反映直观权威的权重功能、代表的民主考虑或具体任务的优先事项,而不是假设单一的划线观点,使得动态观点具有优先性。 最后,对于挑战(3),SAJ-MTL通过将注释器和目标表示物纳入添加剂的MTL架构来实现可引导计算. 避免每平面模型的四极爆炸,使框架能够处理许多利益攸关方群体,而不牺牲预测性能和记忆停滞。

blocks.en:
We evaluate SAJ-MTL on online toxicity detection, a consequential setting wherein demographic disagreements directly shape annotation outcomes. Toxicity judgments are deeply subjective, tied to lived experience, historical context, and group-specific exposure to harm. As prior work shows, language that appears innocuous to one community may be offensive when directed toward another [ 53 , 12 ] . Moreover, when annotators hold negative beliefs about a group, they are less likely to label speech targeting that group as hateful [ 10 ] . Toxicity datasets
frequently employ majority-vote aggregation, which suppresses minority-group opinions and systematically biases models away from those most affected by harmful content [ 11 ] . By considering the relationships between annotator and target demographics, SAJ-MTL produces a more faithful representation of how different communities perceive harm and enables viewpoint prioritization that centers the perspective of those at risk of being harmed. Evaluation on two toxicity datasets show SAJ-MTL improves context-aware understanding of demographically sensitive content and improves prediction.
blocks.zh:
我们评价关于在线毒性检测的SAJ-MTL, 毒性判断具有很深的主观性,与活的经验,历史背景,以及特定群体的伤害暴露有关. 如先前的研究表明,对一个社区似乎无害的语言,如果指向另一个社区,[53,12] 可能是冒犯性的。 此外,当注释者对某一群体持有负面的信仰时,他们不太可能将针对该群体的言论标榜为仇恨[10]. 毒性数据集
经常采用多数投票制,压制少数群体的意见,有系统地偏向那些受有害内容影响最大的人[11]。 通过考虑注释者与目标人口统计之间的关系,SAJ-MTL更忠实地表述了不同社区如何看待伤害,并使人们能够将可能受到伤害者的观点置于优先地位。 对两个毒性数据集的评价显示,SAJ-MTL提高了对人口敏感性内容的上下文认识,并改进了预测。

blocks.en:
Contributions: 1) Joint Stakeholder Modeling . SAJ-MTL explicitly models demographic interactions between annotator, target and content, with generality allowing broad use across diverse subjective annotation tasks with multiple stakeholders. The model dynamically assesses and weighs different, socially-grounded perspectives given specific context rather than an averaged viewpoint. Conditional gradient routing supports sparse samples per task. 2) Disagreement-Aware Protocols . We describe two protocols to systematically model annotator disagreements and preserve diverse viewpoints erased by majority-vote aggregation: Across-Groups (AG) vs. Across-and-Within-Groups (AWG). 3) Scalable MTL . SAJ-MTL reduces scaling complexity from multiplicative to additive w.r.t. group cardinality of annotator and target, ensuring feasibility and cost-effectiveness for
applications with many demographic groups. 4) Better Toxicity Detection . When applied to toxicity detection, SAJ-MTL models how different annotator–target groups perceive harmful language, yielding predictions that respect demographic variation, leading to more context-sensitive toxicity judgments and reduced fairness disparities across groups. 5) Reproducibility . We will share our source code via Github,
including architecture code and detailed experimental protocols.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: We connect research in machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) on annotator disagreement, content relationships, and scalable MTL.
blocks.zh: 我们把机器学习(ML)和自然语言处理(NLP)的研究连接到注释器分歧,内容关系,以及可缩放的MTL上.

blocks.en:
Tasks with Annotator Disagreements. Crowdsourcing and annotation work has repeatedly found structured heterogeneity in labels that correlates with annotator attributes [ 63 ] . Early work explicitly modeled annotator reliability and systematic biases [ 13 , 67 ] while later work extended this to jointly learn annotator confusion matrices with classifiers [ 49 ] .
Even tasks with seemingly objective ground truth are labeled differently depending on the background, expertise, familiarity and lived experiences of the annotators, which is well-documented across domains. Judgments about stove design are highly subjective, with ideal forms varying significantly across the world and socioeconomic groups [ 21 ] . In medical diagnosis, decisions can vary based on a clinician’s training, experience, and normative practices of their professional environment [ 1 ] . Radiologists trained in different clinical settings may legitimately disagree on whether a faint shadow in an X - ray signals pathology or artifact [ 30 ] . In cardiology, recognized symptoms of a heart attack, such as crushing chest pain radiating down the left arm, are historically based on presentations in White male patients, but women and Black patients often present with different or subtler symptoms [ 26 ] .
These examples motivate models that preserve annotator-level variation [ 11 ] .
blocks.zh:
与注释者分歧的任务 。 众包和注释工作在与注释属性相关的标签中多次发现结构异质性[63]. 早期的工作明确模拟了注释者的可靠性和系统性偏差[13,67],而后期的工作则扩展了这一点,以共同学习与分类者的注释混淆矩阵[49].
即使是表面客观的事实真相的任务,其名称也有所不同,这取决于注释者的背景、专长、熟悉程度和生机勃勃的经验,这些经验在各个领域都有充分的记载。 对炉灶设计的判断是高度主观的,理想的形式在世界各地和社会经济团体中差异很大[21]. 在医学诊断方面,可以根据临床医生的培训、经验和专业环境的规范做法,作出不同的决定。 在不同的临床环境中接受过培训的放射学家,对于X-射线信号病理学或文物中的微弱阴影,可能会有合理的分歧[30]. 在心脏病学中,公认的心脏病发作症状,如压扁胸腔疼痛散射到左臂下,历史上都是根据白人男性患者的介绍,但女性和黑人患者经常出现不同或更微妙的症状[26].
这些例子激励了保留注释层变化的模型[11].

blocks.en:
Modeling Annotator-Content Relationship. Recent works model different dimensions of the annotator–content relationship directly in the modeling pipeline [ 63 ] . Jury learning [ 22 ] treat annotators as stakeholders and learns to predict annotator-specific labels.
Personalized classifiers [ 70 ] adapt predictions to an individual annotators’ sensitivity using per-user annotation history, while noise-aware multi-annotator frameworks [ 32 ] estimate per-annotator reliability to denoise labels. These approaches capture individual preference, but none of these models the relationship between demographics of annotators and of another stakeholder (e.g. target) as context-dependent variation.
Most directly related to our work, Fleisig et al. [19] model annotator disagreement for subjective tasks by conditioning on annotator and target identity, serving as a precursor to our approach and a primary baseline.
While prior work demonstrates the value of conditioning on annotator identity, in practice it can be data-hungry or privacy-invasive by requiring per-annotator surveys or identifiers. However, Sachdeva et al. [51] show that annotator behavior in subjective tasks like toxicity prediction can be efficiently modeled by decomposing judgments into independent latent traits (see Appendix A for a psychometric interpretation of SAJ-MTL as a neural generalization of identity-sensitive IRT). Our work contributes to this body of literature by proposing a scalable multi-task learning approach that models the relationship between annotator and target demographics.

个性化分类器 [70] 利用每个用户的注释历史来适应单个注释者的敏感度,而噪声感知多注释器框架 [32] 估计每个注释器的可靠性为凹痕标签. 这些方法反映了个人的偏好,但这些模型中没有一种将注释者的人口统计与另一利害关系方(如目标)的人口统计关系作为依具体情况而定的变异。
与我们的工作最直接相关的是Fleisig等人。 [19] 模型注释员对主观任务持不同意见,以注释员和目标身份为条件,作为我们方法的前身和主要基准.
虽然以前的工作证明了对注释者身份加以限定的价值,但实际上,它可以通过要求每个注释者进行调查或识别资料而造成数据匮乏或隐私入侵。 然而,Sachdeva et al. [51] 表明在毒性预测等主观任务中的注释者行为可以通过将判断分解成独立的潜伏特征来有效模拟(见附录A,关于将SAJ-MTL作为对身份敏感IRT的神经通化的心理分析解释). 我们的工作通过提出一种可扩展的多任务学习方法,模拟注释者与目标人口学之间的关系,为这一系列文献作出了贡献。

blocks.en: Demographic Bias and Fairness in NLP. Models trained on aggregated annotations are well-known to reproduce and even amplify social biases. Sap et al. [53] , Davidson et al. [12] show that marginalized perspectives can be systematically underrepresented when datasets collapse annotations. Dixon et al. [15] highlight disparities in toxicity detection across demographic groups. Studies underscore the importance of fairness-aware modeling approaches that explicitly consider group-level variation.
blocks.zh: NLP的人口偏见与公平. 受过综合说明培训的模型广为人知,可以复制甚至扩大社会偏见。 萨普等人. [53], Davidson等人著. [12] 显示,当数据集崩溃说明时,边缘化视角可能会被系统地低估。 狄克逊等. [15] 强调各人口群体在毒性检测方面的差异。 研究强调了明确考虑群体层面差异的公平意识建模方法的重要性。

blocks.en: Scalability in MTL. Scaling MTL models to many tasks (annotator × \times target heads in our work) is challenging. Naive per-task heads typically leads to multiplicative parameter growth in both memory and runtime [ 5 ] , so recent architectures emphasize parameter-efficiency and sparse conditioning. Adapter modules [ 27 ] and adapter fusion [ 47 ] allow compact per-task updates, while Low-rank adaptation [ 28 ] and prompt/prefix tuning [ 38 ] keep the per-task footprint small. Mixture-of-Experts [ 56 , 18 ] uses learned sparse routing to provide additional model capacity with controlled FLOPs, while multi-gate MoE [ 41 ] and PLE [ 61 ] propose task-specific gating for MTL. Techniques for gradient conflict mitigation [ 69 , 8 ] address optimization interference among tasks and remain an active area of research.
blocks.zh: 缩放(MTL). 将 MTL 模型推广到许多任务( 注释员\\\ 工作时的目标头) 具有挑战性 。 内存和运行时间[5]通常会导致内存和运行时的多态参数增长[5],因此近期的架构强调参数效率以及简陋的配置. 适配器模块[27]和适配器聚变[47]允许每个任务进行紧凑的更新,而低级的适应[28]和即时/前缀调制[38]则保持每个任务脚印的较小. Mixture-of-Experts [56,18] 使用所学的稀疏路由,以受控制的FLOP提供额外的模型容量,而多门MOE [41] 和PLE [61]则为MTL提出任务特异性标注. 梯度冲突缓解技术[69,8]处理任务之间的优化干扰问题,并继续是一个活跃的研究领域。

blocks.en: 3 Methods
blocks.zh: 3个 方法

blocks.en: We now formalize the problem of demographic-aware annotation and introduce our Stakeholder-Aware Joint Multi-Task Learning (SAJ-MTL) framework. After highlighting inherent scalability issues with a naive multi-task formulation, we detail our scalable factorized architecture designed to efficiently capture both annotator and target group conditionality, labeling protocols, training objective and viewpoint prioritization scheme.
blocks.zh: 我们现在将人口意识问题正式化,并介绍我们的利益攸关方-知情联合多任务学习框架。 在以天真的多任务提法强调固有的可伸缩性问题之后,我们详细介绍了我们的可伸缩的因子化结构,这种结构旨在有效抓住注释者和目标群体的条件、标签协议、培训目标和观点优先计划。

blocks.en: 3.1 Notation & Problem Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 标记和问题表述

blocks.en: We formalize the annotation setting as follows. Let X X denote the space of input samples ( e.g. , text comments), which we map to a structured feature representation via a text encoder ( e.g. , BERT [ 14 ] , RoBERTa [ 40 ] , etc. ). Let Y Y denote the label space ( e.g. , toxicity score). Each comment is associated with a structured feature vector x ∈ X x\in X , an annotation label y ∈ Y y\in Y , and metadata about the annotator-group and the target-group (mentioned or implicated in the content). We denote A = { a 1 , a 2 , … , a | A | } A=\{a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{|A|}\} as the set of annotator demographic groups, and T = { t 1 , t 2 , … , t | T | } T=\{t_{1},t_{2},\ldots,t_{|T|}\} as the set of target demographic groups, with cardinality as | A | |A| and | T | |T| respectively.

Each training instance i ∈ N i\in N is a tuple ( x i , a i , t i , y i ) (x_{i},a_{i},t_{i},y_{i}) , where x i ∈ X x_{i}\in X is the content (feature vector of post), a i ∈ A a_{i}\in A is the annotator’s demographic group, t i ∈ T t_{i}\in T is the target’s demographic group, and y i ∈ Y { 0 , 1 } y_{i}\in Y^{\{0,1\}} is the binary judgment noting the label given by annotator a i a_{i} to instance x i x_{i} when considered in relation to target t i t_{i} ( e.g. , is a post hateful towards a particular demographic). We assume the observed label is drawn from a conditional distribution y i ∼ P ⁡ ( y ∣ x i , a i , t i ) y_{i}\sim P(y\mid x_{i},a_{i},t_{i}) , where both annotator- and target-group identities influence the group-conditioned interpretation of the content. This explicitly departs from both traditional single-truth formulations that assume y i ∼ P ⁡ ( y ∣ x i ) y_{i}\sim P(y\mid x_{i}) alone governs labeling, and stakeholder-aware formulations that condition predictions on the content and a single stakeholder at a time.
3.2 Naive Extension of Conditional MTL
blocks.zh: 3.2 条件MTL的自然延伸

blocks.en: Figure 1: Naive All-Pairs SAJ-MTL. Each annotator-target pair ( a , t ) (a,t) is modeled as a separate task and dedicated head, allowing direct learning of pairwise interactions but yielding multiplicative parameter growth and data sparsity for underrepresented pairs.
blocks.zh: 图1:Naive All-Pairs SAJ-MTL. 每个注释者-目标对(a, t) (a, t) 被建模为单独的任务和专注头,可以直接学习对偶的相互作用,但为代表性不足的对对子产生多种参数增长和数据痉挛.

blocks.en:
Gupta et al. [23] ’s CondMTL combines a shared encoder with multiple task-specific prediction heads. One simple way to model demographic variation would be to extend CondMTL with conditional gradient routing, as shown in Fig. 1 , with each prediction head corresponding to
a combination of an annotator group a ∈ A a\in A and a target group t ∈ T t\in T .
While this structure allows the model to learn localized annotator–target interactions directly, it suffers from severe scalability and data sparsity issues. In this naive setup, the number of task-specific parameters grows multiplicatively at a rate of 𝒪 ⁡ ( | A | × | T | ) \mathcal{O}(|A|\times|T|) . Many demographic pairings in real-world settings, including MHS [ 52 ] and KET [ 37 ] , are quite sparse ( e.g. , ∼ \sim 1% of data). This makes it nearly impossible for dedicated all-pair heads to converge effectively without overfitting.

虽然这种结构允许模型直接学习本地化的注释器-目标相互作用,但它有严重的可伸缩性和数据溅射性问题。 在这种天真设定中,任务特定参数的数量以O QQ(| A | T | T | T | T |)的速率成倍增长. 现实世界环境中的许多人口配对,包括MHS[52]和KET[37],都相当稀少(例如,\\sim 1%的数据)。 这使得全神贯注的头脑几乎不可能在不过度调整的情况下有效汇合。

blocks.en: Figure 2: Scalable SAJ-MTL. Annotator and target effects are factorized into independent modules and combined additively. This enables efficient modeling of annotator–target interactions while reducing complexity to linear scaling, improving both parameter efficiency and generalization in sparse settings.
blocks.zh: 图2:可缩放的SAJ-MTL. 注释器和目标效果被分解为独立的模块和加成物. 这使得能够高效地模拟注释者-目标互动,同时将复杂性降低到线性缩放,提高参数效率和在稀有环境中的概括性。

blocks.en: To overcome combinatorial explosion and data sparsity issues, our improved scheme must decouple the annotator-specific variations from the target-specific contexts, while still allowing the model to account for the relationship between them. By factorizing these components, as shown in Fig. 2 , we can achieve a scalable architecture that learns these effects independently and composes them additively. This ensures the model scales efficiently at 𝒪 ⁡ ( | A | + | T | ) \mathcal{O}(|A|+|T|) , sharing general representation knowledge while still effectively modeling the complex, subjective interactions between the annotator and the targeted group.
blocks.zh: 为了克服组合爆炸和数据痉挛问题,我们经过改进的计划必须把针对具体对象的注释员的变异性与特定对象的变异性脱钩,同时仍然允许模型对它们之间的关系进行衡算. 如图2所示,通过将这些组件纳入要素,我们可以实现一个可伸缩的架构,独立地学习这些效应,并以添加剂的方式编曲. 这确保了O QQ(QQ A + + + + T + )\ mathcal{O}(QQA + T +)的模型尺度高效,分享一般代表知识,同时仍然有效模拟注释者与目标群体之间的复杂,主观的互动.

blocks.en: 3.3 Modeling Annotator-Target Conditionality
blocks.zh: 3.3 模拟注释者-目标条件

blocks.en: We model the subjective prediction of input x x , annotated by demographic group a a and referring to target group t t , using separate representations for the input and each stakeholder identity. Specifically, the shared encoder (with parameters ϕ \phi ) produces a content embedding h ϕ ​ ( x ) ∈ ℝ d h_{\phi}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{d} , while learnable embedding layers produce annotator embeddings e a ∈ ℝ d a e_{a}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{a}} , and target embeddings e t ∈ ℝ d t e_{t}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{t}} , corresponding to the demographic groups a a and t t , respectively. These three embedings are then combined through the proposed conditional architecture yielding a stakeholder-conditioned representation: z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) = f c ​ o ​ n ​ d ​ ( h ϕ ​ ( x ) , e a , e t ) z(x,a,t)=f_{cond}(h_{\phi}(x),e_{a},e_{t}) (1) where f c ​ o ​ n ​ d f_{cond} is a conditional parameterization function that composes the three components into a unified latent representation. The function may take various forms depending on modeling priorities. The fused representation is then passed through branch-specific module heads g a , g t g_{a},g_{t} , yielding conditional predictions: f θ ​ ( y ∣ x , a , t ) = softmax ​ [ g a ​ ( z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) ) + g t ​ ( z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) ) ] f_{\theta}(y\mid x,a,t)=\text{softmax}\,[\,g_{a}(z(x,a,t))+g_{t}(z(x,a,t))\,] (2) This enables annotator-target specific losses to backpropagate through the shared encoder h ϕ h_{\phi} and the relevant group-specific embeddings e a e_{a} , e t e_{t} . blocks.en: 3.4 Architectural Overview
blocks.zh: 3.4 建筑概况

blocks.en: SAJ-MTL implements annotator–target conditionality with each annotator–target pair corresponding to a logical task. Parameters are composed from independent annotator- and target-specific modules, rather than instantiated explicitly (see Fig. 3 ). Whereas conventional MTL tasks are predefined and static, SAJ-MTL tasks are conditionally activated based on annotator and target metadata for each labeled instance. We implement the conditional parameterization function f c ​ o ​ n ​ d f_{cond} as a linear additive function to empirically balance expressiveness and computational efficiency. z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) = h ϕ ​ ( x ) + W a ​ e a + W t ​ e t z(x,a,t)=h_{\phi}(x)+W_{a}e_{a}+W_{t}e_{t} (3) Given the conditional representation z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) z(x,a,t) , SAJ-MTL assigns a distinct prediction head to each annotator group a a and a distinct prediction head to each target group t t . Formally, let g a , g t : ℝ d → ℝ k g_{a},g_{t}:\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{k} denote the annotator-specific and target-specific heads, respectively. The final logits for an instance labeled by annotator a a about target group t t are obtained by combining both heads with the conditional representation: ℓ ⁡ ( x , a , t ) = g a ​ ( z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) ) + g t ​ ( z ⁡ ( x , a , t ) ) \ell(x,a,t)=g_{a}(z(x,a,t))+g_{t}(z(x,a,t)) (4) The additive structure allows annotator-related semantic shifts and target-related contextual shifts to contribute independently and interpretably, unlike learning a single classifier conditioned on metadata tokens [ 19 ] , which entangles annotator and target effects for less explicit disagreement modeling.

For each labeled instance ( x i , a i , t i , y i ) (x_{i},a_{i},t_{i},y_{i}) , annotator-target–conditioned logits are produced where the conditional representation z ⁡ ( x i , a i , t i ) z(x_{i},a_{i},t_{i}) includes shared content features and group-specific effects. ℓ ⁡ ( x i , a i , t i ) = g a i ​ ( z ⁡ ( x i , a i , t i ) ) + g t i ​ ( z ⁡ ( x i , a i , t i ) ) \ell(x_{i},a_{i},t_{i})=g_{a_{i}}(z(x_{i},a_{i},t_{i}))+g_{t_{i}}(z(x_{i},a_{i},t_{i})) (5) The model is trained using the conditional negative log-likelihood: ℒ ( θ ) = − 1 N ∑ i = 1 N log f θ ( y i ∣ x i , a i , t i ) = − 1 N ∑ i = 1 N log softmax ( ℓ ( x i , a i , t i ) ) y i \mathcal{L}(\theta)=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\log f_{\theta}(y_{i}\mid x_{i},a_{i},t_{i})=-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\log\text{softmax}\,(\ell(x_{i},a_{i},t_{i}))_{y_{i}} (6) A key feature of SAJ-MTL is selective gradient routing. blocks.en: As a conditional gradient routing model, SAJ-MTL encounters the typical challenge of gradient interference across tasks. However, because SAJ-MTL decomposes annotator and target effects additively, the parameter space naturally reduces conflicting gradients. One may further incorporate MTL optimization techniques such as gradient normalization (GradNorm [ 8 ] ), gradient projection (PCGrad [ 69 ] ) or multi-objective balancing (MGDA [ 55 ] ), to modulate interactions between annotator and target updates. In practice, we find that the additive factorization is stable under standard optimizers such as AdamMax [ 33 ] without requiring explicit multi-task gradient control. To prevent overfitting on small groups and ensure meaningful separation between annotator and target effects, SAJ-MTL applies standard L 2 L_{2} regularization on head parameters, dropout within the dense modules, and norm constraints on the embeddings e a , e t e_{a},e_{t} to prevent representational collapse.
blocks.zh: 作为有条件的梯度路由模型,SAJ-MTL遇到跨任务梯度干扰的典型挑战. 然而,由于SAJ-MTL会以添加剂的方式分解注释器和目标效应,参数空间自然减少相互冲突的梯度. 可以进一步采用梯度正常化(GradNorm [8]),梯度预测(PCGrad [69])或多目标平衡(MGDA [55])等MTL优化技术来调节注释者与目标更新之间的相互作用. 在实践中,我们发现在亚当马克斯[33]等标准优化器下,添加式保理化是稳定的,不需要明确的多任务梯度控制. 为了防止小群体过度适应,并确保在注释者与目标效果之间有意义的分离,SAJ-MTL在头部参数上适用标准L 2 L_{2}规范化,在密集模块内放弃,以及嵌入e a, e a},e_{t}的规范约束,以防止代表崩溃.

blocks.en: 3.6 Viewpoint Prioritization Mechanism
blocks.zh: 3.6 视点优先化机制

blocks.en: Subjective annotation tasks often require privileging certain perspectives over others, especially in contexts where lived experience or group-specific harm confers epistemic authority. To support such socially grounded decision-making, SAJ-MTL incorporates a viewpoint prioritization mechanism that modulates predictions based on the relationship between annotator and target groups. This allows the model to flexibly reflect platform policies, application goals, or normative choices about whose perspective should guide evaluation.
blocks.zh: 主观的注释任务往往要求将某些观点置于其他观点之上,特别是在生活经验或特定群体的伤害赋予认知权威的情况下。 为了支持这种基于社会的决策,SAJ-MTL采用了一种观点优先机制,根据注释者和目标群体之间的关系来调整预测。 这使该模式能够灵活地反映平台政策、应用目标或关于谁的观点应指导评价的规范性选择。

blocks.en: Given the conditional prediction function f θ ​ ( y ∣ x , a , t ) f_{\theta}(y\mid x,a,t) , a prioritization weight π ⁡ ( a , t ) \pi(a,t) specifies the influence of annotator group a a when assessing content involving target group t t . The prioritization function: π : A × T → [ 0 , 1 ] \pi:A\times T\rightarrow[0,1] is constrained to satisfy ∑ a ∈ A π ⁡ ( a , t ) = 1 \sum_{a\in A}\pi(a,t)=1 for each target group t t . At inference time, the model produces an aggregate prediction by marginalizing over annotator perspectives under the chosen weighting scheme: y ^ = P ⁡ ( y ∣ x , t ) = arg ⁡ max ⁡ ∑ a ∈ A y ⁡ π ⁡ ( a , t ) ​ f θ ​ ( y ∣ x , a , t ) \hat{y}=P(y\mid x,t)=\arg\max_{y}\sum_{a\in A}\pi(a,t)f_{\theta}(y\mid x,a,t) (7) This general formulation allows SAJ-MTL to implement a variety of prioritization strategies proposed in prior literature on stakeholder-aware and participatory modeling [ 36 , 58 , 31 , 68 ] . blocks.en: 4.1 Evaluation Scenarios and Datasets

blocks.en: We evaluate SAJ-MTL on two datasets for toxicity and hate-related classification that include annotator demographics. Both datasets are well-suited for studying annotator disagreement, with multiple labels per instance and systematic variation across demographic groups. We distinguish two evaluation settings. First, the Annotated-Target Scenario (Section 5.1 ) provides a controlled-setting with definitively known targets via human annotation, i.e. annotations indicating which demographic group is the target of a post. The Measuring Hate Speech (MHS) corpus [ 52 ] supports such evaluation. Practical deployment, however, requires target detection. This is the Detected-Target Scenario , a more realistic and noisy evaluation condition (Section 5.2 ). This particularly matters for SAJ-MTL, since the model conditions on target-group identity during inference. Together, these two settings enable us to assess both the upper-bound performance of the model under known target conditions vs. practical effectiveness in more realistic settings. For the target detection scenario, we detect targets using a custom detection module (see Appendix D ), then report results on MHS (ignoring human-annotated target labels) and on the KET dataset [ 37 ] (which lacks human-annotated targets).

blocks.en: 4.4 Data Pipeline Protocols
blocks.zh: 4.4 (中文(简体) ). 数据管道协议

blocks.en: Subjective annotation datasets often contain multiple labels per instance that capture variation both across groups and within the same group. To formally model this, we consider two labeling strategies distinguishing how labels are indexed and used by SAJ-MTL: AG (Across-Groups) vs. AWG (Across-and-Within-Groups). This distinction is critical for learning differences in subjective data. The AG strategy focuses on disparate belief i.e. , modeling systematic differences in labeling behavior between distinct groups. In contrast, the AWG strategy addresses the ecological fallacy of assuming group-level trends apply uniformly to all individuals by explicitly modeling variation both across groups and within each group. This enables labels to capture the fact that not all members within a group necessarily agree. Such an approach enables a granular representation that avoids over-generalization while still capturing inter-group differences.
blocks.zh: 主观注释数据集往往包含每个实例的多个标签,这些标签既能捕捉不同组别之间,又能捕捉同一组内的差异. 为了形成正式的模式,我们考虑两种标签战略,区分标签的索引方式和SAJ-MTL的使用方式:AG(跨集团)与特设工作组(跨集团和与集团)。 这种区分对于学习主观数据的差异至关重要. AG战略侧重于不同的信仰,即模拟不同群体之间标签行为的系统差异。 与此相反,特设工作组的战略处理假设群体一级的趋势对所有个人统一适用的生态谬误,明确模拟群体之间和每个群体内部的差异。 这使标签能够捕捉到并非一个集团所有成员都必然同意的事实。 这种方法能够使颗粒化的表述方式避免过度概括,同时仍然能够反映各组之间的差异。

blocks.en: AG (Across-Groups): Each sample receives a single, group-consolidated label per group representing the group’s average/majority perspective. Different label instances for the same sample therefore correspond strictly to different groups, treating each group’s judgment as a cohesive unit. This approach captures systematic differences between groups but does not account for individual disagreement within a group.
blocks.zh: AG( 跨组): 每个样本每个组获得一个单一的、分组合并的标签,代表组的平均/多数观点。 因此,同一样本的不同标签情况严格对应不同的群体,将每个群体的判断视为一个团结单位。 这种方法捕捉到各群体之间的系统性差异,但并不说明某一群体内部的个人分歧。

blocks.en: AWG (Across-and-Within-Groups): A single sample can have multiple labels from within the same demographic group, in addition to labels from different groups. This allows the model to see several differing opinions from individuals in the same group. This captures both inter-group and intra-group differences, reflecting the rich spectrum of individual disagreement that exists inside any demographic category.
blocks.zh: 特设工作组(集团间和集团间): 单一样本除了来自不同群体的标签外,还可以有来自同一人口组内的多个标签. 这使得模型可以看到一些与同一群体中的个人不同的意见. 这既反映了群体之间的分歧,也反映了群体内部的分歧,反映出任何人口类别中都存在着丰富的个人分歧。

blocks.en: AG captures systematic differences across demographic groups by learning from a single representative label per group, whereas AWG additionally preserves disagreement among individuals within the same demographic group. Because within-group disagreement provides additional information about the diversity of stakeholder perspectives, we hypothesize that AWG will learn richer stakeholder-conditioned representations and consequently achieve better predictive performance than AG. Our experiments in Section 5 evaluate whether preserving this additional disagreement translates into measurable improvements.

blocks.en: Table 1 reports classification results on the MHS dataset with human-annotated targets, and reports both micro- and macro-averaged metrics. SAJ-MTL consistently outperforms baselines, showing the benefit of explicitly modeling annotator–target relationships. In regard to SAJ-MTL variants, AWG labeling performs better than AG labeling, reaching a (macro/micro)-F1 of (0.65, 0.64), highlighting the benefit of modeling both across-group disagreements and within-group variation, which are lost when annotations are aggregated or treated as homogeneous within each demographic group. In terms of baselines, CondMTL, which models only the target demographic as a task, performs substantially worse across all metrics. This suggests that modeling the annotator group is critical for some subjective tasks such as toxicity detection, where judgments depend strongly on the relationship between the annotator and the content they are annotating. The inclusion of annotator demographics serve as an additional dimension for the model to learn a better toxicity boundary. Baseline TextAug performs better than CondMTL for most groups, but remains significantly below SAJ-MTL. This suggests that while text augmentation allows annotator metadata to influence the encoder representation, it does not provide explicit structural modeling of annotator–target interactions. Consequently, TextAug appears to struggle to disentangle how different communities interpret the same content.

We next examine whether modeling demographic disagreement into the framework improves fairness across groups, measured using the Equal Opportunity (EO) gap ( Section 4.3 ) on MHS. By learning separate annotator- and target-specific representations, the model can capture differences in how communities perceive harmful language without forcing a single universal decision boundary. blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: Role of Disagreement in Annotation . A recurring theme across subjective NLP tasks is that annotator disagreement is not merely noise but a reflection of societal and individual variation in lived experience. Literature increasingly emphasizes that collapsing multiple labels into a single ground truth can erase meaningful minority interpretations [ 44 ] and misrepresent the underlying construct being annotated. Davani et al. [11] show that aggregating labels via majority vote systematically suppresses minority demographic variation, effectively erasing the valid perspectives of marginalized groups from the training signal. Gordon et al. [22] argue that heterogeneous judgments should not be discarded, as they encode essential information about how different demographic stakeholders distinctively perceive harm, offensiveness, and context. Fleisig et al. [19] highlight that relying on a forced consensus often leads models astray; they show that retaining un-aggregated annotations allows classifiers to learn robustly even when the majority opinion is contextually flawed or socially biased. The proposed methodology contributes to this body of work through a scalable multi-task learning framework for modeling disagreement in annotation tasks, which demonstrates significant improvements for modeling toxicity detection.

blocks.en: Interpreting Viewpoint Prioritization in Practice. While our model can represent a wide array of demographic perspectives, the decision of which viewpoint to prioritize remains a task-specific normative choice. In SAJ-MTL, this prioritization is formalized through a weighting function π ⁡ ( a , t ) \pi(a,t) , reflecting epistemic, pluralistic, policy-driven, or task-specific decisions about whose perspective should matter most. Following the perspective-aware framework of Basile et al. [3] , our work supports a shift beyond a single gold standard toward a system that accounts for disaggregated human perspectives. The flexible design of π ⁡ ( a , t ) \pi(a,t) allows practitioners to encode diverse priorities at inference time, integrating annotators’ group membership as a primary component of the model’s prediction logic rather than treating it solely as a feature of data collection. This approach directly addresses the findings of Prabhakaran et al. [48] , who demonstrated that standard label aggregation (like majority voting) often introduces systematic biases by over-representing majority perspectives and obscuring the lived experiences of minority groups. In our framework, prioritization is not used to correct the model, but to enable explicit normative choices of how different voices are accounted for. For example, it can be used to center the voices of those with the highest stake in the outcome. In the context of anti-Asian hate speech, for instance, the model can be configured to prioritize the perspective of Asian annotators, ensuring the detection threshold aligns with the community most directly impacted. This flexibility enables a more equitable and context-aware moderation strategy that adapts to different normative choices without requiring retraining. SAJ-MTL thus operationalizes the principle that interpretation depends not only on what is being annotated, but on who is annotating and whom the content targets, without requiring policy priorities to affect the training pipeline.
blocks.zh: 解释观点点在实践中的优先顺序。 虽然我们的模式可以代表广泛的人口观点,但决定优先排序仍然是针对具体任务的规范选择。 在SAJ-MTL中,这种优先排序是通过一个权重函数__(a, t)\pi(a, t)来正式确定的,它反映了对谁的观点最要紧的认知、多元、政策驱动或具体任务决定。 遵循Basile等人的观点认识框架。 [3],我们的工作支持从一个单一的金本位转向一个考虑到人类分类观点的体系. π(a, t)\pi(a, t)的灵活设计使从业人员能够在推论时间编码各种优先事项,将注释者群体成员作为模型预测逻辑的主要组成部分,而不是仅仅将其作为数据收集的一个特征。 这种方法直接涉及Prabhakaran等人的调查结果。 [48],他们证明,标准标签汇总(与多数投票一样)往往带有系统性的偏见,过度代表多数人的观点,并掩盖少数群体的实际经历。 在我们的框架中,优先次序不是用来纠正模式的,而是用来对如何考虑不同的声音作出明确的规范性选择。 例如,它可以用来将结果中利害关系最高者的声音集中起来. 例如,在反亚洲仇恨言论方面,可以对该模式进行配置,以优先考虑亚洲注释者的观点,确保发现阈值与受影响最大的社区保持一致。 这种灵活性能够使一种更加公平和了解具体情况的温和战略适应不同的规范性选择,而不需要再培训。 因此,SAJ-MTL将这一原则付诸实施,即解释不仅取决于附加说明的内容,而且取决于说明者及其内容目标,而不需要政策优先事项来影响培训程序。

blocks.en:
Generalization to other tasks. Although in this work we explicitly focused on toxicity detection, the SAJ-MTL framework naturally generalizes to many subjective or context-sensitive tasks in NLP and beyond. Tasks such as stance classification, sentiment analysis, misinformation verification, and even medical image analysis have well-documented sources of demographic variation in annotation. For instance,
in medical image analysis, diagnoses can vary systematically based on a clinician’s training, experience, and the demographic presentation of the patient. Rather than treating such clinical disagreement as noise, SAJ-MTL could be used to factorize these expertise and patient-context variables to preserve critical diagnostic signals [ 71 ] . As noted by Sorensen et al. [59] , as AI systems are increasingly deployed in global contexts, they must move away from average human preferences toward a value-pluralistic stance. Because SAJ-MTL’s conditional structure simply combines shared semantic encoders with annotator- and target-specific branches, it does not assume anything special about toxicity labels and can be applied wherever group-conditioned interpretation is relevant. Moreover, because inference-time aggregation is decoupled from model training, domain experts in these diverse fields can tailor viewpoint prioritization to reflect domain-specific norms, regulatory structures, or governance criteria without retraining the underlying model.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: Human annotations in subjective tasks often reflect socially grounded disagreement rather than objective ground truth. Single-truth or majority-voted paradigms treat such variation as noise, discarding valuable signal about annotator and target-group perspectives. To address this, we introduced SAJ-MTL, a joint annotator–target–aware multi-task learning framework that explicitly models interactions between annotators’ demographics and content. Using a factorized conditional architecture with selective gradient routing, SAJ-MTL captures structured cross- and within-group variation while scaling linearly with the number of groups and requiring only minimal group-membership information in order to preserve privacy. A flexible viewpoint prioritization mechanism further decouples disagreement modeling from deployment-time choices, allowing practitioners to encode epistemic authority, pluralism, or policy constraints without retraining. Applied to toxicity detection, SAJ-MTL improves macro-level performance on demographic-sensitive content and reduces group-level disparities, all without explicit fairness objectives.
blocks.zh: 人类在主观任务中的描述往往反映了基于社会的分歧,而不是客观的真理。 单一事实或多数投票的范式将这种变化视为噪音、丢弃关于注释者和目标群体观点的宝贵信号。 为了解决这个问题,我们引入了SAJ-MTL,这是一个联合的注释者-目标-认识的多任务学习框架,明确模拟了注释者的人口和内容之间的相互作用。 使用带有选择性梯度路由的阶梯化条件架构,SAJ-MTL捕捉结构化的跨组和组内变异,同时与组数线性地缩放,只需要最低限度的组成员信息,以保持隐私. 一个灵活的观点优先安排机制将分歧模式与部署时间的选择进一步脱钩,使从业人员能够在不进行再培训的情况下,将认知权威、多元化或政策限制编码。 在毒性检测方面,SAJ-MTL改进了对人口敏感含量的宏观性能,缩小了群体层面的差距,但都没有明确的公平目标。

blocks.en: Beyond toxicity, SAJ-MTL offers a general template for learning from subjective annotations where stakeholder perspectives vary systematically. The additive factorization of annotator and target groups suggests a natural extension to a stakeholder triad that incorporates author demographics, as recent works show that author dialect and identity also shape toxicity perception [ 7 , 42 ] . Integrating such signals additively would capture triadic dynamics while maintaining our privacy-preserving, group-level formulation. More broadly, future work could relax rigid group categories by learning hierarchical or latent group structures, enabling the model to discover intersectional identities obscured by broad demographic labels. Finally, SAJ-MTL’s architecture is well-suited to multi-modal applications: applied to medical imaging with a Vision Transformer encoder, it could reconcile systematic diagnostic disagreements across clinical traditions or specialties, by treating divergent expert judgments as signal rather than noise.
blocks.zh: 除了毒性之外,SAJ-MTL还提供了一个从主观说明中学习的一般模板,在主观说明中,利益攸关方的观点有系统差异。 注释员和目标群体的添加性要素化表明,将自然延伸至一个包含作者人口统计的利益攸关方三合一,因为最近的作品表明作者方言和身份也塑造了毒性感知[7,42]. 以添加剂方式整合这些信号将捕捉三维动态,同时保持我们的隐私保护、群体一级配方。 更广泛地说,今后的工作可以通过学习等级或潜在群体结构来放宽僵硬的团体类别,使模型能够发现被广义的人口标签所掩盖的交叉身份。 最后,SAJ-MTL的架构非常适合多种模式的应用:适用于带有视觉变形器编码器的医学成像,它可以通过将不同的专家判断视为信号而不是噪音来调和临床传统或专业的系统性诊断分歧。

blocks.en: 8 Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 8 道德考虑

blocks.en: The ethical stakes of modeling annotator disagreement are significant. Without explicit design choices, ML systems risk implicitly weighing majority viewpoints, thereby amplifying harms to marginalized or under-represented groups and reinforcing pre-existing biases [ 53 , 12 ] . Still, decisions around how groups are defined, aggregated, or weighted require careful ethical consideration. Across application domains, anchoring these decisions on domain-knowledge, and engaging in participatory design practices may be important avenues to ensure their relevance and legitimacy. Additionally, it is important to note that there is a risk of misuse. It could be possible to define viewpoint prioritization functions that perpetuate or exacerbate marginalization by purposefully centering privileged viewpoints. Thus, transparency regarding viewpoint prioritization mechanisms deployed is essential.
blocks.zh: 建模注释者分歧的道德利益是重大的。 如果没有明确的设计选择, ML系统就可能隐含地权衡多数观点,从而扩大对边缘化或代表性不足群体的伤害,并强化先前存在的偏见[53、12]。 然而,关于如何界定、汇总或加权的团体的决定需要认真的道德考虑。 在整个应用领域,将这些决定置于域知识以及参与设计做法上,可能是确保其相关性和合法性的重要途径。 此外,必须指出存在滥用的风险。 通过有目的地集中特权观点,可以确定使边缘化永久化或加剧边缘化的确定优先事项的职能。 因此,在所部署的轻重缓急安排机制方面,透明度至关重要。

blocks.en: The proposed methodology does not explicitly enforce fairness. Instead, fairness benefits stem from improvements in modeling. This is, however, not guaranteed to happen, and it is essential to explicitly evaluate fairness performance, as illustrated in our experiments. In sensitive domains such as toxicity detection, minimizing performance gaps is not merely an algorithmic optimization metric, but a necessary safeguard against asymmetric harms. Errors may disproportionately affect i) the author of content, via unfair over-moderation or mischarecterization, and ii) the communities targeted by that content, via failure to filter out or appropriately react to harmful content. Careful evaluation across stakeholder groups is therefore required and necessary to avoid reinforcing existing social inequities.
blocks.zh: 拟议方法没有明确执行公平。 相反,公平的好处来自模型的改进。 然而,正如我们的实验所表明的那样,这不能保证会发生,必须明确评价公平表现。 在毒性检测等敏感领域,最大限度地缩小性能差距不仅是算法优化的衡量标准,而且是防止不对称伤害的必要保障。 错误可能不成比例地影响(一) 内容的作者,其方式是不公平的过度修改或错误地查抄;和(二) 该内容所针对的社区,其方式是对有害内容没有过滤或作出适当反应。 因此,需要并有必要对利益攸关方群体进行认真评价,以避免加剧现有的社会不平等。

blocks.en: Our experiments rely exclusively on publicly available datasets [ 52 , 37 ] , and no additional human participants were recruited or annotations collected. We use the datasets subject to their appropriate access and usage conditions. The use of annotator demographic information introduces privacy and representation concerns. Although our methodology operates on group-level demographic attributes, such information may still be sensitive in some scenarios [ 60 , 2 , 66 ] , and its use in deployed ML systems should therefore be subject to appropriate privacy guardrails, informed consent where applicable, and restrictions against discriminatory profiling.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验完全依靠公开的数据集[52,37],没有招聘额外的人类参与者或收集说明. 我们使用数据集,但必须具备适当的访问和使用条件。 使用注释员的人口信息提出了隐私和代表性问题。 虽然我们的方法是针对群体一级的人口特征,但在某些情况下,这种信息可能仍然很敏感[60、2、66],因此,在所部署的ML系统中使用这种信息应受到适当的隐私保护装置、酌情获得知情同意以及禁止歧视性定性的限制。

blocks.en: Appendix C Dataset Details
blocks.zh: 附录C 数据集 细节

blocks.en: We use the Measuring Hate Speech (MHS) corpus [ 52 ] , available via the HuggingFace library [ 16 ] , which includes 135,556 posts sourced from YouTube, Twitter and Reddit. Each post is annotated by one or more human annotators and includes: i) the inferred demograhic group(s) targeted by the post; ii) self-reported group-demographic attributes of the annotators; and iii) a binary toxicity label indicating whether the content is perceived as toxic or non-toxic towards the inferred target. Although the dataset has seven demographic race groups as target, we keep only four demographic groups - Asian , Black , Latinx and White , and omit three others ( Middle-Eastern , Native-American and Pacific-Islander ). This is due to extremely sparse annotator–target ( A i , T j A_{i},T_{j} ) pair instances in the three omitted groups. For included groups, both annotators and targets were drawn as shown in Table 7 . Because individual posts may be annotated by multiple annotators, we perform the train–validation–test split at the post level to prevent content leakage across splits. Specifically, posts are randomly partitioned into 70%, 10%, and 20% subsets for training, validation, and testing, respectively. All annotations associated with a given post are assigned to the same split. Within each split, a post may still have multiple annotator labels, which allows us to model annotator-specific variation while preserving strict separation of textual content across splits. The dataset exhibits substantial variation in the frequency with which different demographic groups are targeted. For example, the Black community represents the statistical majority among targeted groups.

blocks.zh: 附录D 目标检测

blocks.en: In many real-world deployment settings, the demographic group targeted by a post may not be explicitly available and must instead be inferred automatically. While MHS provides human-annotated target-groups, such targets will typically need to be automatically (noisily) detected. Consequently, stakeholder-aware prediction systems often rely on an auxiliary model to estimate target identities before downstream classification. We perform automatic target detection to evaluate SAJ-MTL under this more realistic setting, to assess the robustness of stakeholder-aware modeling when demographic target assignments contain errors.
blocks.zh: 在许多现实世界的部署环境中,员额所针对的人口群体可能无法明确提供,必须自动推断。 虽然卫生部提供附加说明的目标群体,但这类目标通常需要自动(无声)检测。 因此,利益攸关者认识的预测系统往往依赖辅助模型在下游分类之前估计目标身份。 我们进行自动目标检测,以便在这种更现实的设定下评估SAJ-MTL,评估在人口目标任务存在错误时利益攸关方意识模型的健全性。

blocks.en: Similar to the protocol by Fleisig et al. [19] , we use an custom target detection model. For their work, they used a GPT-2 based module fine-tuned on a different dataset. However, note that different platforms and sources of data come with their own length formats, audience demographics, moderation policies etc . Hence to prevent such artifacts originating from decoupling, our custom target detection model uses the same underlying text encoder architecture as the downstream models and is trained independently using available target annotations where applicable i.e. , the MHS dataset in our case. This makes the entire pipeline coupled in terms of data source and text representation. To avoid information leakage, target detection and downstream toxicity classification are trained separately on the same splits. The text encoder is followed by dense neuron layers (512, 128, 64 neurons respectively), with relu activation, added biases and dropout rate of 0.1 to prevent model overfitting. The layers end in | T | |T| classification nodes, each with sigmoid activation, no biases and 0.5 threshold. Given that a single post can target one or more groups simultaneously, we use weighted Binary Cross Entropy (wBCE) as our loss to optimize overall error. The rounded detection accuracy rates for the demographic groups were as follows: Asian: 81%, Black: 87%, Latinx: 82%, White: 77%, with the corresponding confusion matrix shown in Table 9 .

blocks.en: Appendix F Scalability of SAJ-MTL
blocks.zh: 附录F SAJ-MTL的可扩展性

blocks.en: A key design goal of SAJ-MTL is to scale nominally with increasing numbers of annotator and target groups. However, in the naive design as shown in Fig. 1 , this leads to multiplicative parameter growth of 𝒪 ⁡ ( | A | × | T | ) \mathcal{O}(|A|\times|T|) . SAJ-MTL addresses this challenge through a factorized parameterization in which annotator and target effects are learned independently and composed additively. With a single shared encoder, a small set of annotator and target embeddings, the total number of group-specific parameters scales additively as ( 𝒪 ⁡ ( | A | + | T | ) \mathcal{O}(|A|+|T|) ) (Fig. 2 ). This ensures tractability even in settings with dozens of annotator groups or highly diverse target identities. Concretely, rather than instantiating a separate head or parameter block for each ( a , t ) (a,t) pair, SAJ-MTL reuses a single shared encoder and a set of small annotator and target modules, allowing the model to represent structured disagreement without incurring combinatorial cost.

blocks.en: In practice, this design leverages parameter-efficient model design ideas from [ 27 , 28 ] . Beyond memory scalability, this parameterization enhances computational efficiency. Because only the annotator and target modules relevant to an example receive gradient updates, SAJ-MTL amortizes shared backbone updates and computation across tasks. By conditioning predictions on small learned embeddings rather than duplicating large network components, batch-level throughput remains stable even as the number of groups grows. Compared to frameworks such as Mixture-of-Experts [ 56 , 41 ] , which introduce routing and communication overhead, SAJ-MTL achieves scalability with minimal architectural overhead for embedding lookup and head routing. This design ensures fairness-aware modeling remains deployable in resource-constrained environments. Finally, additive factorization promotes generalization across sparse groups. Groups with limited labeled examples benefit from the shared encoder while still receiving individualized modeling capacity. Conversely, well-represented groups can develop more specialized representations through repeated branch-specific updates. This makes SAJ-MTL robust to the long-tailed, heterogeneous distributions common in subjective labeling settings.
blocks.zh: 在实践中,这种设计利用[27,28]的参数效率模型设计理念. 除了内存的可扩展性,这种参数化提高了计算效率. 因为只有与实例相关的注释器和目标模块会收到梯度更新,所以SAJ-MTL分期摊销共享主干线更新和跨任务计算. 批量的吞吐量即使随着组数的增加也保持稳定。 与采用路由和通信高通航线的Mixture-of-Experts[56,41]等框架相比,SAJ-MTL实现了可伸缩性,最小的建筑高通航线用于嵌入外观和头部路由. 这种设计确保了公平意识的建模在资源有限的环境中仍然可以部署。 最后,添加性保理会促进稀有群体的普遍化。 标签上的例子有限的团体从共享编码器中受益,同时仍然获得个性化的模型制作能力. 反之,代表人数充足的群体可以通过重复提供具体分支的最新情况,形成更专业的表述。 这使得SAJ-MTL对主观标签设置中常见的长尾异形分布具有强性.

blocks.en: Fig. 7 shows a simulation of memory scaling across three models vs. some annotator-target pairings. All models have a fixed DistilBERT weight as minimum memory and additional dense layers. When the number of groups is one, we see that CondMTL and SAJ-MTL have effectively the same memory, since they end up with the same architecture. With increasing groups, the quadratic scaling kicks in and we see the memory for naive SAJ-MTL quickly saturating towards GPU limit, a phenomena exhibited by any standard MTL architecture. However, the Scalable SAJ-MTL variant almost grows asymptotically w.r.t. CondMTL (which just considers target group), all the while capturing interactions across both annotator-target groups.
